title: A2 Integrated Physics Project
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed formative text exercises; not an A2 capstone assessment.

sources.title: Virtual cart: observation sheet
paragraphs: An instructor runs a virtual straight-line cart model for a class. The timer starts at zero seconds. The program displays 0.0 m at 0 s, 1.5 m at 1 s, 3.0 m at 2 s and 4.5 m at 3 s. The student checks the time label and records each position in a table. The cart moves at a constant modeled speed during the displayed interval. The student writes “Position (m)” beside the vertical axis and “Time (s)” beside the horizontal axis. These are virtual model values, not measurements from a real laboratory. There is no displayed value at four seconds. A future value can be predicted only if an additional motion assumption is stated.

sources.title: Temperature monitoring note
paragraphs: A student opens a safe virtual temperature model. At 0 min, the displayed temperature is 30 °C. At 2 min, it is 28 °C. At 4 min, it is 26 °C. The student records the values with units. The line decreases over the shown interval. The student tells a partner, “The temperature went down by four degrees Celsius in four minutes.” The student does not claim that 24 °C was measured at six minutes because the graph ends at four minutes. The model helps practise the language of observations, not physical temperature measurements.

sources.title: Resistance experiment preparation
paragraphs: A virtual circuit contains an ideal resistor, a variable voltage source and a current display. The student first checks the connection in the simulation. The model gives 0.10 A at 2 V, 0.20 A at 4 V and 0.30 A at 6 V. The current increases as the voltage increases. The student draws a table and labels both quantities. The circuit is an ideal educational model; no real wire or electrical source is connected. In the results paragraph, the student writes “The modeled current increased with voltage.” The student avoids claiming that the results apply to all components.

sources.title: Small report: a virtual pendulum
paragraphs: A student uses a simple digital pendulum model and records three displayed periods: 1.2 s, 1.3 s and 1.2 s. The report has four sections: apparatus, procedure, results and conclusion. In the procedure, the student writes that the timer was started and the displayed period was recorded three times. The results section contains the three numbers with the unit s. The conclusion states that the model showed similar but not identical readings. The student does not call these real experimental readings. In a short oral summary, the student says, “We used a virtual pendulum, recorded three periods and compared the displayed values.”
